Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: The records office maintains a controlled filing system for institutional paperwork. Intake documents are assigned accession numbers, logged in the master register with date-stamped entries, and routed to designated custodians via approved channels. Each entry links source, custodian, and date fields, forming a verifiable paper trail.

2) What occurred: The actor accessed the maintenance register for the affected airframe and located the part-history record for the unapproved component. The actor altered the component identifier field to match an approved part number, modified the installation date field to a prior date, and changed the source-of-supply field to a named approved vendor account. The actor filed the amended record through the internal document channel, replacing the prior entry, and marked the record as verified in the status field. The actor transmitted the amended part history via a named account to the regulator-facing filing channel.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor used a named user account with register-edit access. The altered artifacts included: the maintenance register entry (accession number, part number field, date field, source field, status field); the part-history certificate (part number, serial number, installation date); the vendor correspondence (a dated record from a named account); and the filing receipt (a dated record confirming the submission through a named channel).

4) Indicators & artifacts: Mismatch between the part serial number and the original manufacturer certificate. Date field on the installation entry predating the component's documented supply date. Source field referencing a vendor account inconsistent with the approved-supply register for that part number. Version history showing a single bulk edit rather than incremental updates. Filing receipt date postdating the amended installation date. Absence of a prior supersession entry for the original record in the master register.
